- When sentiment is low (≤0.25) and forecast drops sharply, model tends to underestimate — adjust downward by 2–5% for next period.  
- After a strong upward spike in price (e.g., >+10% from prior peak), model often overshoots — cap forecast at +5% above recent peak.  
- If sentiment is high (≥0.4) and price is falling, model overcorrects downward — add 1–3% upward bias to counteract mean reversion.  
- In early horizon (e.g., 1–3 days ahead), model underestimates volatility — increase forecast by 1–3% if sentiment is volatile (±0.3–0.5).  
- If 30-day forecast shows consistent downward trend with sentiment <0.2, model often fails to capture mean reversion — add 2–4% upward correction in middle of forecast.  
- When sentiment is flat or neutral (0.2–0.4) and price is trending, model lags — shift forecast 1–2 days ahead to align with sentiment momentum.
